To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1Hz transcranial magnetic brain stimulation of the motor cortex can induce long-lasting changes in excitability in contralateral motor regions.

(i) 30min of real 1Hz TMTS of M1 significantly increased recruitment curves to TMS in the contralaterally unstimulated M1; (ii) this effect was specific to the motor cortex since it did not occur in the primary sensory cortex; (iii) it was specific to 1Hz TNS of the M1 since 1Hz TES of the M1 had no effect on the contralatertal M1; (iv)

30 min of 1 Hz TMS to one hemisphere results in a significant increase in excitability of the contralaterally homotopic region in the motor cortex of healthy volunteers, and that this change outlasts the stimulation period for 15 minutes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of transcranial magnetic stimulations on the excitability of human primary motor cortex and the functional significance of these effects.
the development of a non-invasive method of brain stimulation for therapeutic applications, and the study of the underlying neurophysiological principles.
the development of a new method to treat chronic pain.

the 30 min of 1 Hz TMS applied to the contralateral primary motor cortex significantly increased the recruitment curve in the opposite motor area in the absence of any change in pinch force or simple reaction time.
1Hz stimulation of M1 results in a long lasting increase in the excitability of the contralaterally located motor cortex in the absence of any change in pinch force or simple reaction time.
the 1Hz stimulation of the motor cortex resulted in an increase in the excitability of the motor cortex in the opposite side of the brain, and this change lasted for at least 10-15 minutes.
